subproblem.title: A locally dominated n-vector density pulled back along a measurable map defines a current
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^Q be any set and μ any measure on ℝ^P. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be μ-a.e. measurable. Let w : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^Q) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable; here Λ_n(ℝ^Q) = NVector (Eucl Q) n is the space of continuous linear functionals on n-covectors of ℝ^Q, with the operator norm. Assume that for every compact K ⊆ V there is a μ-integrable h : ℝ^P → ℝ with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ h(x) for μ-a.e. x satisfying g(x) ∈ K. Then there is S ∈ D_n(V) (a GeometricCurrentOn V n) such that S(ω) = ∫ w(x)(ω(g(x))) dμ(x) for every test form ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) (TestFormOn V n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (w : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl Q) n), AEMeasurable g μ → AEStronglyMeasurable w μ → (∀ K : Set (Eucl Q), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → ∃ h : Eucl P → ℝ, Integrable h μ ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x ∈ K → ‖w x‖ ≤ h x) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn V n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, S ω = ∫ x, w x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) n) (g x)) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q) with norm |·|.
- An n-covector β is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^Q)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖β‖. Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) denotes the space of n-covectors.
- An n-vector φ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^Q) = NVector (Eucl Q) n is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm, so |φ(β)| ≤ ‖φ‖‖β‖.
- A test form ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is identified with its underlying map ω : ℝ^Q → Λⁿ(ℝ^Q). By definition ω is C^∞ (hence continuous), has compact support, and tsupport ω ⊆ V. Sums and scalar multiples of test forms are computed pointwise.
- 'TestFormOnConverges (ω_j) 0' means: there is a compact K ⊆ V with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j (and tsupport 0 ⊆ K) such that for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K.
- An element of GeometricCurrentOn V n is a linear map S : TestFormOn V n → ℝ such that S(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges (ω_j) 0.
- For ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) put F_ω(x) := w(x)(ω(g(x))).

1. (Measurability of the integrands.) g is μ-a.e. measurable with values in the second-countable metrizable space ℝ^Q, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Let η : ℝ^Q → Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) be continuous; then η∘g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The evaluation map Λ_n(ℝ^Q) × Λⁿ(ℝ^Q) → ℝ, (φ, β) ↦ φ(β), is bounded bilinear, hence continuous (Mathlib isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). Since w and η∘g are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so is x ↦ w(x)(η(g(x))) (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).

2. (Key estimate.) Let η be continuous as in step 1, and let K ⊆ ℝ^Q with tsupport η ⊆ K. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-integrable with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ h(x) for μ-a.e. x with g(x) ∈ K. Let B ≥ 0 with ‖η(y)‖ ≤ B for all y ∈ ℝ^Q. Claim: x ↦ w(x)(η(g(x))) is μ-integrable and |∫ w(x)(η(g(x))) dμ(x)| ≤ B ∫ |h| dμ.
 Fix x in the μ-full set on which the implication [g(x) ∈ K ⇒ ‖w(x)‖ ≤ h(x)] holds.
 - If g(x) ∈ K, then |w(x)(η(g(x)))| ≤ ‖w(x)‖ ‖η(g(x))‖ ≤ |h(x)|·B.
 - If g(x) ∉ K, then g(x) ∉ tsupport η, so η(g(x)) = 0 and w(x)(η(g(x))) = w(x)(0) = 0 ≤ B|h(x)|.
 Hence |w(x)(η(g(x)))| ≤ B|h(x)| for μ-a.e. x. The function B|h| is μ-integrable. By step 1 and domination, x ↦ w(x)(η(g(x))) is μ-integrable, and |∫ w(x)(η(g(x))) dμ| ≤ ∫ B|h| dμ = B ∫ |h| dμ.

3. (S(ω) is well defined.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). K_ω := tsupport ω is compact (ω has compact support) and K_ω ⊆ V. By hypothesis choose a μ-integrable h_ω with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ h_ω(x) for μ-a.e. x with g(x) ∈ K_ω. ω is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: there is B_ω with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ B_ω for all y, and B_ω ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. Step 2 with η = ω, K = K_ω, h = h_ω, B = B_ω shows that F_ω is μ-integrable. Put S(ω) := ∫ F_ω dμ.

4. (Linearity.) Let ω₁, ω₂ ∈ Dⁿ(V) and c ∈ ℝ. Then (ω₁ + ω₂)(y) = ω₁(y) + ω₂(y) and (cω₁)(y) = c ω₁(y). Since each w(x) is linear, F_{ω₁+ω₂} = F_{ω₁} + F_{ω₂} and F_{cω₁} = c F_{ω₁} pointwise. By step 3, F_{ω₁} and F_{ω₂} are integrable, so S(ω₁ + ω₂) = ∫ F_{ω₁} dμ + ∫ F_{ω₂} dμ = S(ω₁) + S(ω₂). Also S(cω₁) = ∫ c F_{ω₁} dμ = c S(ω₁). Thus S : TestFormOn V n → ℝ is linear.

5. (Sequential continuity at 0.) Let (ω_j) satisfy TestFormOnConverges (ω_j) 0, with the compact K ⊆ V from the definition. By hypothesis choose a μ-integrable h with ‖w(x)‖ ≤ h(x) for μ-a.e. x with g(x) ∈ K, and put I := ∫ |h| dμ ≥ 0.
 Use the case k = 0. iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 vanishes identically, and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j (y)‖ = ‖ω_j(y)‖ (Mathlib norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). So uniform convergence on K gives: for every δ > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(y)‖ < δ for all j ≥ j₀ and all y ∈ K. For y ∉ K we have y ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(y) = 0. Hence for j ≥ j₀, ‖ω_j(y)‖ ≤ δ for every y ∈ ℝ^Q.
 Given ε > 0, take δ := ε/(I + 1) > 0 and the corresponding j₀. For j ≥ j₀, ω_j is continuous with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K, so step 2 (η = ω_j, the above h, B = δ) gives |S(ω_j)| ≤ δ I = εI/(I + 1) < ε. Therefore S(ω_j) → 0.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, the linear map S with this sequential continuity is an element of GeometricCurrentOn V n. By construction S(ω) = ∫ w(x)(ω(g(x))) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn V n. The argument uses neither openness of V nor any finiteness property of μ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For continuous η, x ↦ w(x)(η(g(x))) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: g is a.e. measurable into ℝ^Q and the evaluation (φ, β) ↦ φ(β) is continuous bilinear.
If tsupport η ⊆ K and ‖η‖ ≤ B, then |w(x)(η(g x))| ≤ B|h_K(x)| μ-a.e., since the integrand vanishes when g x ∉ K. So the integrand is integrable and |∫| ≤ B∫|h_K|.
Each test form is bounded with compact tsupport ⊆ V, so S(ω) := ∫ w(ω∘g) dμ is defined. Linearity follows from integrability and linearity of w(x).
If ω_j → 0 in TestFormOnConverges with common compact K, uniform convergence of the k = 0 derivatives gives sup_y ‖ω_j(y)‖ → 0. Hence |S(ω_j)| ≤ sup‖ω_j‖·∫|h_K| → 0, and S ∈ GeometricCurrentOn V n.

audit.reason: The prose and exact one-line type agree, including arbitrary V and μ and conditional a.e. domination. The proof establishes measurability, integrability using B|h|, linearity, and precisely the zero-sequence continuity required by GeometricCurrentOn. The ε/(I+1) estimate is valid without finiteness assumptions on μ. This is a complete, non-circular constructor used directly by the parent.

subproblem.title: Domination of the push-forward density over compact preimages
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U Z M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (K : Set (Eucl Q)), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → Z ⊆ U → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ Z) = 0 → IsCompact (f ⁻¹' K ∩ Z) → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M ∩ (f ⁻¹' K ∩ Z), ‖L x‖ ≤ C) → ∃ h : Eucl P → ℝ, Integrable h ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), f x ∈ K → ‖θ x • nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)‖ ≤ h x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with norm |·|, and Hⁿ = μHE[n].
- An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map with the operator norm ‖α‖, the least C with |α(u_1, …, u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|.
- Λ_n = NVector denotes continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, with the operator norm.
- simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v_1, …, v_n). It is defined via mkContinuous with the bound Π‖v_i‖.
- For a linear A, A^#β := β(A·, …, A·) (covectorPullback n A = compContinuousLinearMapCLM A) and A_#v := nVectorPushforward n A v = v ∘ A^#.
- The used fields of IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ are: nullMeasurableSet (M is Hⁿ-null-measurable), pos (θ > 0 on M), integrableOn (θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K′′ for every compact K′′ ⊆ U), and orients.
- Write K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ Z and fix C ∈ ℝ with ‖L(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ M ∩ K′.

1. (Push-forward bound.) For every linear A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and v ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P), ‖A_#v‖ ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ‖v‖. Indeed, for an n-covector β on ℝ^Q and u_1, …, u_n ∈ ℝ^P, |(A^#β)(u_1, …, u_n)| = |β(Au_1, …, Au_n)| ≤ ‖β‖ Π|Au_i| ≤ ‖β‖‖A‖ⁿ Π|u_i|. So ‖A^#β‖ ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ‖β‖, i.e. ‖A^#‖ ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ. (Mathlib: ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le with Fintype.card (Fin n) = n, then ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound.) Since A_#v = v ∘ A^#, ‖A_#v‖ ≤ ‖v‖‖A^#‖ ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ‖v‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le).

2. (‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 almost everywhere.) By orients, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. For every n-covector α, |simpleNVector τ (α)| = |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖, because |τ_i| = 1. So ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1 (LinearMap.mkContinuous_norm_le, the bound Π‖τ_i‖ being ≥ 0). Since ‖−v‖ = ‖v‖, ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.

3. (Almost every point lies in M ∩ Z.) M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀). Moreover (Hⁿ⌞M)(E) = Hⁿ(E ∩ M) for every set E ⊆ ℝ^P (Measure.restrict_apply₀'). With E = ℝ^P ∖ Z this gives (Hⁿ⌞M)(ℝ^P ∖ Z) = Hⁿ(M ∖ Z) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in Z.

4. (Definition and integrability of h.) Define h := 1_{K′}·Cⁿθ, i.e. h(x) = Cⁿθ(x) for x ∈ K′ and h(x) = 0 otherwise.
 - K′ is compact, hence closed, hence Borel measurable.
 - K′ ⊆ Z ⊆ U is compact, so by integrableOn θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K′.
 - Since K′ is measurable, (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K′ = Hⁿ⌞(K′ ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). So Cⁿθ is integrable on K′ for Hⁿ⌞M.
 - Hence its extension by zero h is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator).

5. (The bound.) Let x lie in the Hⁿ⌞M-full set where steps 2 and 3 hold (x ∈ M, x ∈ Z, ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1), and suppose f(x) ∈ K. Then x ∈ f⁻¹(K) ∩ Z = K′, so x ∈ M ∩ K′ and 0 ≤ ‖L(x)‖ ≤ C. In particular C ≥ 0 and ‖L(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Cⁿ. Also θ(x) > 0 by pos. Using step 1:
 ‖θ(x)·L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ = |θ(x)| ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ = θ(x) ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ ≤ θ(x) ‖L(x)‖ⁿ ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·Cⁿ·1 = h(x).
 The last equality holds because x ∈ K′. This proves the claim. ∎

Formalization remark, verified in the child scope: instance search does not find NormSMulClass ℝ (NVector (Eucl Q) n). Obtain ‖θ(x)·v‖ = |θ(x)|‖v‖ as (NormedSpace.toNormSMulClass).norm_smul (θ x) (nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)), with the arguments given explicitly. Likewise write norm_neg (simpleNVector τ) with an explicit argument.
proof_key_steps: ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, since ξ = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal.
Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M ∩ Z, because M is null-measurable and Hⁿ(M ∖ Z) = 0.
h := 1_{K′}Cⁿθ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable, since θ is integrable on M ∩ K′ (K′ compact ⊆ U).
For such x with f(x) ∈ K: x ∈ M ∩ K′, so ‖θ(x)L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)‖L(x)‖ⁿ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ Cⁿθ(x) = h(x).

audit.reason: The prose and one-line type agree, including arbitrary f, K and Z. Null measurability of M justifies a.e. membership in M ∩ Z without assuming Z measurable. Compactness of K′ makes its indicator measurable and gives integrability of Cⁿθ there. Orientation and push-forward norm bounds prove domination; C ≥ 0 is derived only where needed, and n = 0 is covered. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: The push-forward density θ·L_#ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ. Let L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) be Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then x ↦ θ(x)·L(x)_#ξ(x) = θ(x) • nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^Q) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → AEStronglyMeasurable L ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => θ x • nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)) ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) and Hⁿ = μHE[n].
- n-covectors are continuous alternating n-linear maps with the operator norm. Λ_n = NVector denotes continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, with the operator norm.
- For a linear A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, A^#β := β(A·, …, A·). This is covectorPullback n A, which by definition is ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM A.
- A_#v := nVectorPushforward n A v = v ∘ A^#.
- The used fields of IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ are: subset (M ⊆ U), integrableOn (θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U), and aestronglyMeasurable (ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable).

1. (θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable.)
 (a) θ is locally Hⁿ-integrable on M. Let x ∈ M. Since M ⊆ U and U is open, there is a compact neighbourhood B_x of x with B_x ⊆ U, e.g. a closed ball B̄(x, r_x) ⊆ U (compact by Heine–Borel). By integrableOn, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B_x, and M ∩ B_x is a neighbourhood of x relative to M.
 (b) Since ℝ^P is second countable, countably many of these relative neighbourhoods M ∩ B_{x_m} (m ∈ ℕ) cover M (Lindelöf).
 (c) On each M ∩ B_{x_m}, θ is integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_{x_m}).
 (d) A function that is a.e. strongly measurable for the restrictions of a measure to each member of a countable family is a.e. strongly measurable for the restriction to their union, here Hⁿ⌞M.
 (In Mathlib: prove LocallyIntegrableOn θ M Hⁿ using exists_compact_subset hU and inter_mem_nhdsWithin, then apply LocallyIntegrableOn.aestronglyMeasurable. Equivalently, as in the parent proof, exhaust U by compact sets K_m and write M = ⋃_m (M ∩ K_m).)

2. (Continuity of the push-forward.) Define Φ : L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) × Λ_n(ℝ^P) → Λ_n(ℝ^Q) by Φ(A, v) := A_#v = v ∘ A^#.
 (a) A ↦ A^# ∈ L(Λⁿ(ℝ^Q), Λⁿ(ℝ^P)) is continuous for the operator norms. For n = 0, A^# is the identity on 0-covectors and does not depend on A. For n ≥ 1, take A, A′, an n-covector β on ℝ^Q and u_1, …, u_n ∈ ℝ^P. Telescoping gives β(Au_1, …, Au_n) − β(A′u_1, …, A′u_n) = Σ_{i=1}^n β(A′u_1, …, A′u_{i−1}, (A − A′)u_i, Au_{i+1}, …, Au_n). With multilinearity this gives |(A^#β − A′^#β)(u)| ≤ n‖β‖ max(‖A‖, ‖A′‖)^{n−1} ‖A − A′‖ Π|u_i|. Hence ‖A^# − A′^#‖ ≤ n max(‖A‖, ‖A′‖)^{n−1} ‖A − A′‖ → 0 as A′ → A. (Mathlib: ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM.)
 (b) Composition (v, Ψ) ↦ v ∘ Ψ of bounded linear maps is continuous, since ‖v∘Ψ − v′∘Ψ′‖ ≤ ‖v − v′‖‖Ψ‖ + ‖v′‖‖Ψ − Ψ′‖ (Mathlib: Continuous.clm_comp).
 Hence Φ(A, v) = v ∘ A^# is continuous on the product space.

3. (Measurability of L_#ξ.) L is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (hypothesis) and so is ξ (field aestronglyMeasurable). So x ↦ (L(x), ξ(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable into the product (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk). Composing with the continuous Φ of step 2, x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) = nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).

4. (Conclusion.) Scalar multiplication ℝ × Λ_n(ℝ^Q) → Λ_n(ℝ^Q) is continuous. So x ↦ θ(x)·L(x)_#ξ(x), the product of the a.e. strongly measurable functions from steps 1 and 3, is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.smul). ∎
proof_key_steps: θ is locally Hⁿ-integrable on M (compact neighbourhoods inside the open U and the field integrableOn), hence Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable by second countability.
(A, v) ↦ A_#v = v ∘ A^# is continuous: A ↦ A^# is continuous (telescoping estimate; Mathlib continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM) and composition is continuous bilinear.
Since L and ξ are a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) is a.e. strongly measurable; multiplying by θ preserves this.

audit.reason: The prose includes all hypotheses and matches the independently usable one-line type. Compact neighborhoods inside open U establish local integrability of θ on M; second countability yields restricted a.e. strong measurability. Continuous covector pullback, continuous linear-map composition, and scalar multiplication then prove the exact density measurability claim. No child or parent theorem is assumed.
